topic: hsc exam results to be published on october 29
headline: HSC results to be published October 29
summary: Over 1.27 million students await their higher secondary certificates as the date is finalized by the Inter Education Board Coordination Committee.
details: The results for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on Thursday, October 29.
Professor Syed Akteruzzaman, Chairman of the Dhaka Education Board and President of the Inter Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the date on Saturday night.
The education boards had previously proposed a window between October 25 and 29 to the Ministry of Education, which has now been finalized as the 29th.
A total of 1,270,583 students, including both regular and irregular candidates, appeared for the exams which began on July 2.
While the vast majority of students sat for the exams, a significant number of candidates remained absent.

topic: 8.8 million taka found in Shahjalal shrine donation box
headline_marked: BDT 8.8 million [[found in donation boxes of Hazrat Shahjalal (R) shrine]]
headline: BDT 8.8 million found in donation boxes of Hazrat Shahjalal (R) shrine
summary: Along with Bangladeshi Taka, gold, silver, and currencies from multiple countries were recovered during the counting process in Sylhet.
details: Authorities recovered BDT 8.86 million from the sealed historical pots and newly installed donation boxes at the Hazrat Shahjalal (R) shrine in Sylhet.
The counting process took place on Saturday under the supervision of district administration officials, with the final amount announced by Deputy Commissioner Abdullah Al Mamun.

In addition to the cash, officials found 1.875 bhori of gold jewelry, 3.13 bhori of silver, and currencies from various countries including the UK, India, Thailand, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, USA, Qatar, and Hong Kong.
This was the fourth round of counting. Previous rounds yielded BDT 8.89 million on September 19, nearly BDT 10 million on August 15, and BDT 1.7 million on June 22.
The funds are being deposited into a newly opened bank account managed by the Deputy Commissioner's office to ensure financial transparency.

The initiative to seal the donation boxes and introduce a new management system began in June under the former Deputy Commissioner, following a move to ensure accountability in the shrine's income and expenditure.
A 13-member committee, formed under the initiative of Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muqtadir, is now overseeing the financial management of the shrine.
The committee recently decided that 35% of the funds will be used for the shrine's development and 65% for other operational expenses.
caption:
BDT 8.8 million, gold, and foreign currencies found in a shrine's donation box!

Authorities recovered BDT 8.86 million from the sealed historical pots and newly installed donation boxes at the Hazrat Shahjalal (R) shrine in Sylhet.

The counting process took place on Saturday under the supervision of district administration officials, with the final amount announced by Deputy Commissioner Abdullah Al Mamun.

In addition to the cash, officials found 1.875 bhori of gold jewelry, 3.13 bhori of silver, and currencies from various countries including the UK, India, Thailand, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, USA, Qatar, and Hong Kong.

This was the fourth round of counting. Previous rounds yielded BDT 8.89 million on September 19, nearly BDT 10 million on August 15, and BDT 1.7 million on June 22.

The funds are being deposited into a newly opened bank account managed by the Deputy Commissioner's office to ensure financial transparency.

The initiative to seal the donation boxes and introduce a new management system began in June under the former Deputy Commissioner, following a move to ensure accountability in the shrine's income and expenditure.

A 13-member committee, formed under the initiative of Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muqtadir, is now overseeing the financial management of the shrine.

The committee recently decided that 35% of the funds will be used for the shrine's development and 65% for other operational expenses.
